answer: Give every identity a slow climb, not a free pass. A new agent starts at the foot of a ledge with tiny transaction limits, and its standing only rises as a long, publicly auditable river of honest work flows past — each completed job a jade token of proof that cannot be transferred or sold. Cloning an identity resets the climb to zero, so an attacker must pay the full time-and-compute cost for every fake, while one honest agent pays it just once.
